newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says won't touch pensions without debate.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says won't touch pensions without debate.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday he would not touch Italian pensions without long and deep debate.
Prodi, speaking a news conference on a visit to Germany, said: "Right from the start of my mandate I have said clearly that I cannot change pensions without long and deep discussion."

All Italian welfare spending was concentrated on pensions, "we spend less on health, we don't have unemployment subsidies, therefore I won't touch pensions without a long and deep discussion,' he said.

"In 15 days there will be the results of a study by a committee which has worked on the possibilities (on pensions) then the debate will start. But I will not give a solution which is not analysed, thought out, discussed," he said.
Reporters asked Prodi about the Italian government's relations with the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose parliamentary support is vital to Prodi.
Prodi replied that "having something to do with Refoundation isn't simple. There is debate but up to now we have carried out tough policy with the support of Refoundation."

"I think they understand what's at stake in the case of pensions as well," he said, adding there had been long debate over the future of state telecommunications holding Stet, which was then resolved.
Stet's proposed privatisation has been repeatedly delayed and is now expected to take place late in 1997.
